body:
OBSERVED 2026-08-09. Diagnosis only — the FIX is owned by the CWNG FRONTEND session
(SPA UI/UX sweep). Recorded here because it is readiness evidence for the root-flip
decision, on an axis the parity audit (F-f1159f) cannot see.

ORIGIN: the operator, unprompted, on the SPA's main surface — "the 'Read Now' and edit
buttons are pretty ugly and look not part of the thing." That is a first-hand
ordinary-user reaction to the default catalog view, and it is the same class of
evidence as the Aoife report: a real reaction finding a readiness gap that
feature-coverage greps cannot.

Verified in the tree and in a real browser against cwn-local:

1. NEITHER CONTROL HAS A RESTING STATE. `.readNow` and `.quickEditBtn` are both
   `opacity: 0`, revealed only by `.wrap:hover` / `:focus-within`
   (BookCard.module.css ~285, ~365). On pointer devices the controls do not exist
   until the card is hovered, so the affordance does not merely look weak — it is
   absent until you are already pointing at it.

2. THE EDIT CONTROL WEARS TOKENS FOR A SURFACE IT IS NOT ON. It consumes
   --cover-control-bg/fg/border, documented at tokens.css:58-63 as: "Cover artwork is
   uncontrolled content. Controls over it use a deliberately opaque,
   palette-independent backing so their contrast never depends on the image below."
   The pencil sits in the action row BELOW the cover, on the card surface. In light
   themes that renders an opaque near-black pill with a white hairline border on a
   light card. This is the most likely single cause of "not part of the thing" — it is
   correctly styled for the overlay context and is not in it.

3. A SHARED BUTTON PRIMITIVE EXISTS AND IS UNUSED HERE. components/Button.tsx offers
   variant primary|ghost|danger and size sm|md. BookCard.tsx imports neither it nor its
   CSS and hand-rolls both controls. The card is the most-seen surface in the app, so
   the component that most needed the system is the one that opted out of it.

4. MEASURED GEOMETRY (real browser, not read off CSS): readNow 132x32, radius 10px,
   border 0, bg --accent-soft, color --accent-text. Pencil 24x24, radius full, 1px
   border. No shared height, radius family, or border logic.

5. ACCENT COLLISION, CONFIRMED VISUALLY. The cover hover ring and the primary action
   are the same amber. In the dark card-hover frame the ring is thick and bright and
   wins; "Read now" reads as a caption under it. Deciding what amber is FOR on this
   card is the real design call.

TWO THINGS NOT TO "FIX":
- Touch is already correct. `@media (any-hover: none), (any-pointer: coarse)` sets both
  controls to 44x44 and opacity 1. The defect is pointer-device only.
- tokens.css:36-39 records that --accent as text on --accent-soft is 3.95:1 and
  --accent-text clears AA. `.readNow` uses --accent-text correctly; simplifying to
  --accent would look tidier and silently regress SC 1.4.3.

SCOPE NOTE: `quickEdit` is opt-in — only Catalog.tsx:978 and AdvancedSearch.tsx:255
pass it, so the pencil does not render on every grid.

WHY IT BELONGS IN THE READINESS FILE: F-f1159f measures what is ABSENT from the SPA.
This measures what is PRESENT and incoherent. Both are ordinary-user readiness, and a
flip decision taken on feature coverage alone would miss this entirely.
title: BookCard bypasses the Button primitive and dresses the edit control in cover-overlay tokens
